snippet.title: The Weird Reason Giraffes Have The Same Number of Neck Bones As You
snippet.description:

See, all mammal species except for three have exactly seven cervical vertebrae. And the reason for this is long and complicated, and also includes some cancer. So let's get into it!

snippet.title: The Soldiers Who Glowed In The Dark 🦠
snippet.description:
In 1862, soldiers started glowing in the dark... and it actually saved their lives.

You see, during the American Civil War, soldiers fighting in the Battle of Shiloh noticed something strange…

Some of their wounds began glowing blue.
But what was even more interesting - was that soldiers with glowing wounds seemed to survive more often.

They called this mysterious light the “Angel’s Glow”, and believed it was divine protection.

Doctors were baffled. And for over 100 years the mystery remained unsolved until a 17-year-old high-school student cracked the case.

He discovered that the battlefield soil was home to a rare bioluminescent bacterium called Photorhabdus luminescens.

The bacteria flourished in their wounds… and released powerful natural antibiotics that prevented deadly infections.

snippet.title: The Summer Camp That Turned Kids Into Enemies 😯
snippet.description:
What if you could turn normal kids into enemies…in just five days?

In 1954, psychologist Muzafer Sherif brought 22 average boys to a summer camp in Oklahoma. But this was no ordinary summer camp… it was a psychological experiment designed to answer one terrifying question: How easy is it to turn ordinary people into enemies?

The experiment unfolded in 3 steps:

First, Sherif split the boys into two groups: the Eagles and the Rattlers, and kept them apart for a week.
Each team bonded, created flags, and a group identity.

Then Sherif introduced contests - baseball, tug-of-war, treasure hunts - where only the winners got prizes.
And that’s when everything spiraled out of control.

The teams began behaving badly towards each other. Stealing each other’s supplies, shouting insults, and even burning each other’s flags.

The researchers tried to restore peace with shared meals, and movie nights but none of it worked.
The hatred only grew stronger.

Finally, Sherif began the last step of the experiment. He created fake emergencies that the boys couldn’t solve alone: the camp’s water supply “broke”, the food truck got “stuck” in the mud. So the teams had to unite and ended up proving that the only way to end tribalism is through a shared goal.

snippet.title: How to turn a fifteen-dollar debt into a billion-dollar mistake 📎
snippet.description:
So this guy invented the safety pin, but what he did next cost him billions 

In 1849, inventor Walter Hunt had a problem.

He was $15 in debt and needed money fast.

So he sat down with a piece of brass wire - and in just a few hours, invented the modern safety pin.

The new design achieved two things:
The spring created constant pressure
And the clasp prevented the pin from poking users.

And because it was made from a single piece of metal, it was cheap, strong, and nearly impossible to break.

So Hunt patented the design.

But then made the biggest mistake of his life.

Since he was desperate for cash, he sold the manufacturing rights outright.

Shortly after - the safety pin would go on to be manufactured by the billions - making billions of dollars.

But how much was Walter paid? 

Just a one-time payment of $400.
